facts.text: Fenton lies mostly in Genesee County, with small portions in Oakland and Livingston counties, making it one of two Michigan municipalities that span three counties.
The City of Fenton was incorporated from Fenton Township, and the city and township are administratively separate.
According to local legend, William M. Fenton and Robert LeRoy settled the naming of the town in a poker game, with the town named for the winner and the main street named for the loser.
Millpond Park is a 4-acre park next to Fenton City Hall on the Shiawassee River at 301 S. Leroy Street, with a gazebo, the dam, picnic areas and a war memorial.
Mill Pond Park and Rackham Park sit across Leroy Street from each other in downtown Fenton, and a pedestrian path runs along the Shiawassee River through Rackham Park.

Bush Park, one of Fenton's largest parks, has an entrance on North Leroy Street at Fifth Street, and the Shiawassee River runs through the park, which includes a gazebo, a pavilion and a small island.
Jinglefest, the Fenton and Linden Regional Chamber of Commerce's December holiday event in Fenton, includes a lighted holiday parade followed by a community tree lighting and fireworks.
Lake Fenton, the lake once known as Long Lake, lies just north of the city, and its southern end is within the City of Fenton.
US 23 runs north and south through the west side of the city as a freeway.

christmas-light-installation.title: Fenton Christmas Light Installation | Holiday Light Service
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation in Fenton, MI, including lakefront homes. Rooflines, tree wraps and shrubs, installed, serviced and removed. Free estimates.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Fenton, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Roofline, tree and shrub lighting for Fenton homes, planned to look right from the street and, on the lake, from the water.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: A home on Lake Fenton has two fronts: the side facing the street and the side facing the water. A display that only covers the driveway view leaves half the house dark from the lake, so for waterfront homes we design both elevations, lighting the lake-facing roofline and shoreline trees where they make sense. Reflected in open water or fresh snow, a clean warm-white roofline carries a long way. Away from the lake, the priorities shift to front rooflines, the shrubs along the entry and the trees that frame the house. Whatever the setting, we install with care, keep the display working through the season and take it down after the holidays, with a bucket truck on hand for tall trees and high peaks.
considerations: For waterfront homes, we study the property from the water as well as from the road. Lighting the lake-facing roofline and shoreline trees gives the house presence across the lake and makes the view from inside feel like part of the design.
Wind and weather on open lots

Lots that face open water catch more wind than sheltered streets. We secure runs and tree wraps with that in mind and plan around spots where snow and ice tend to build up. If something shifts mid-season, that is what in-season service is for.

At Jinglefest in December, a lighted parade leads into the community tree lighting and fireworks. If you would like your own roofline lit before that evening, get in touch in early fall. Most installs are scheduled between October and early December, and an early booking keeps more of the calendar open.
faq: Do you install Christmas lights on Lake Fenton homes?

Yes. Homes on and around Lake Fenton are part of our service area, along with the rest of the city and Fenton Township. We plan lakefront designs for both the street and water sides. Mention that you are on the water when you call (248) 756-8915 or request a free estimate.
Does it matter which county my Fenton address is in?

Not for us. Fenton reaches into Genesee, Oakland and Livingston counties, and our service area covers all three. The city and Fenton Township are separate governments, but we install in both, and your estimate is based on the home rather than the jurisdiction.
Should the lake side get the same lighting as the street side?

Not necessarily. The street side is seen up close by visitors, while the lake side is usually seen from across the water, where bold lines carry better than fine detail. We design each side for the distance it is viewed from, and your free estimate shows both, along with what is included for installation, in-season service and takedown.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Fenton Commercial Holiday Lighting | Holiday Light Service
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Commercial holiday lighting for Fenton, MI: riverside storefronts, offices, HOA entrances and managed properties, installed and serviced. Free estimates.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Fenton, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Storefront outlines, entry lighting, bistro strings and tree wraps for downtown Fenton businesses, offices and subdivision entrances.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Downtown Fenton has something many business districts lack: the Shiawassee River running right through it, with Millpond Park beside City Hall on South Leroy Street and Rackham Park across the street. A riverside downtown looks its finest when nearby storefronts are lit with the same care. Outlined facades and windows, a wrapped tree by the door and bistro strings over a patio or walkway all suit the shops and offices here. Come December, the Chamber's Jinglefest adds a lighted parade and community tree lighting to the calendar, and a lit storefront fits right into that season. Beyond downtown, we light offices, managed properties and subdivision entrances across Fenton and Fenton Township.
considerations: Downtown businesses share the view with the river parks, so a clean, warm display suits the setting better than a crowded one. We design around each facade's lines, windows and entries, and we coordinate with the building owner when the storefront is part of a larger building.

If you want your business lit for holiday shopping and Jinglefest, start planning as summer winds down. The install window usually opens in October and closes in early December, and the businesses that book first have the most dates to choose from.

Fenton sits where Genesee, Oakland and Livingston counties meet, and we work in all three. Property managers and businesses with more than one location in the area can keep one lighting partner and one consistent look across every site.
faq: Do you light businesses in downtown Fenton?

Yes. Fenton is in our service area, downtown and beyond. Call (248) 756-8915 or send a quote request with the address and a note about the building, and we will follow up to arrange a free estimate for the design, installation, in-season service and takedown.
Can you light an HOA or subdivision entrance in Fenton?

Yes. Subdivision and HOA entrances are one of the work types we handle. The goal is an entrance that looks deliberate: the sign clearly lit, the nearest trees wrapped and the plantings tying it together. The board or management company gets a design and scope it can review and vote on.
Do you install bistro lighting for patios and walkways?

Yes. Bistro string lighting is one of the work types we install, and it suits patios, walkways and outdoor seating areas well. In a downtown this close to the river it adds warmth without clutter, and higher runs are hung from our bucket truck.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Lighting in Fenton, MI | Holiday Light Service
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent roofline lighting in Fenton, MI, from lake homes to in-town rooflines. App-controlled for holidays, game days and every night. Free estimates.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Permanent roofline lighting, controlled from your phone and ready for Christmas, summer nights and every evening in between.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Permanent lighting pays off most where a house is seen all year, and around Lake Fenton that means every season. After one installation along the eaves, you run it from your phone: soft white on a summer evening, red, white and blue for the Fourth of July, orange through October and a full Christmas scene in December. On a lakefront home we plan the lake-facing roofline as carefully as the street side, since that is the view from the water and from neighbors across it. In town, it does the same quiet work on any roofline, with no ladders at either end of the holidays.
considerations: Permanent lighting is not only a winter feature. On warm evenings it can outline the house in soft white, add color for a Fourth of July gathering or match a team on game day, so the system gets use well beyond a few weeks in December.

On a lake home, the roofline facing the water can matter as much as the one facing the road. We weigh both before recommending where the lighting runs, and we keep the hardware discreet so the house looks tidy by day from either side.

When Jinglefest's lighted parade and tree lighting come around in December, a permanent roofline can switch to a full holiday scene from your phone. The house is ready the moment you decide it should be, with nothing to hang in the cold.
faq: Is permanent lighting available in Fenton and Fenton Township?

Yes. Homes across the city, around Lake Fenton and in Fenton Township can all get permanent, app-controlled roofline lighting from us. Start with a free estimate, by phone at (248) 756-8915 or through the quote form, and we will plan around your roofline and the way you want to use it.
What colors and effects can I use?

The app lets you set steady colors, warm white or holiday scenes and switch between them whenever you like. Common choices include warm white for everyday accent lighting, team colors on game day and seasonal color for Halloween, the Fourth of July and Christmas.
Can I see the plan before committing?

Yes. Your free estimate lays out the design, including which roofline sections will be lit on the street side and, for lake homes, the water side. You can review the plan, ask questions and decide when you are ready.
